 The Orlando Magic are making a statement by beating the defending champion New York Knicks without Paolo Banchero, who sat due to injury. Jeremy Brener | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source New York Knicks forward OG Anunoby and Orlando Magic center Wendell Carter Jr. are separated. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In this story:
 Orlando Magic ORLANDO, Fla. — The Orlando Magic are in the win column for the first time this season after beating the defending champion New York Knicks on the road by a score of 111-102.
--> ORLANDO, Fla. — The Orlando Magic are in the win column for the first time this season after beating the defending champion New York Knicks on the road by a score of 111-102.
 After news broke that star player Paolo Banchero would be out for the next several weeks due to a high ankle sprain, Orlando came into this game as a big underdog . They put the adversity behind them, even after trailing 12-0 in the first 5 minutes of the game. From there, they were in the driver's seat for the rest of the way and pulled it out on top. 
--> After news broke that star player Paolo Banchero would be out for the next several weeks due to a high ankle sprain, Orlando came into this game as a big underdog . They put the adversity behind them, even after trailing 12-0 in the first 5 minutes of the game. From there, they were in the driver's seat for the rest of the way and pulled it out on top. 
 They went toe-to-toe with the defending champions, and it even got chippy at times, but the Magic picked up a much-needed victory to spark some momentum for them after losing their first two games at home.

 Winner: Franz Wagner
--> Winner: Franz Wagner
 Orlando Magic forward Franz Wagner looks on against the Minnesota Timberwolves. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With Paolo Banchero out due to a high ankle sprain, Franz Wagner was expected to step up and take charge for the Magic. He did just that, scoring 23 points while grabbing 13 rebounds and dishing out nine assists in the team's victory.
--> With Paolo Banchero out due to a high ankle sprain, Franz Wagner was expected to step up and take charge for the Magic. He did just that, scoring 23 points while grabbing 13 rebounds and dishing out nine assists in the team's victory.
 Wagner is going to have to play that alpha role for the next several weeks, and this game was proof that he can do just that, even when the odds are stacked against them. The Magic were trailing going into the fourth quarter, but their comeback is a beacon of hope amidst a dark start to the season.

 Winner: Anthony Black
--> Winner: Anthony Black
 Orlando Magic guard Anthony Black poses for a picture during media day. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Anthony Black missed the first two games of the year with an ankle sprain of his own, but he made his presence known in his first game of the season against the Knicks. He was splashing threes left and right off the bench, and his impact for Orlando was needed in this victory. Getting Black back in the rotation is huge for the Magic, and they are happy to have him back.

 Loser: Jase Richardson
--> Loser: Jase Richardson
 Orlando Magic guard Jase Richardson looks on against the Minnesota Timberwolves. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Magic made a somewhat surprising decision to promote point guard Jase Richardson to the starting lineup, but he showed early why that may have been a mistake. The Magic trailed 12-0 out of the gate, all with Richardson on the floor. Once he subbed out, the Magic outscored the Knicks 21-16 for the remainder of the frame. Richardson was a team-low -24, and it was proof that he isn't ready for that kind of role.

 Loser: Goga Bitadze
--> Loser: Goga Bitadze
 Orlando Magic center Goga Bitadze warmups prior to the game against the New York Knicks. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After playing backup center minutes for the past two games, Goga Bitadze was a DNP-CD for the Magic against the Knicks. This likely had to do with the matchup against the Knicks, which was more geared toward Karl Anthony Towns, who usually lines up on the perimeter. Still, it is a slight concern that he wasn't in the rotation. We'll see how that develops when the team takes a two-game trip to Toronto.
